transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Sethi (Redwood CSM), Jonah Miller (Peregrine Head of ML), Asha Patel (Peregrine Dir Eng), Ben Yoon (FinOps), Sara Kim (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Review of last quarter usage, cost spike in July, and reliability incidents (cache stampede on inference nodes)
- Discussed tradeoffs between Hosted bursts vs Dedicated reserved capacity for upcoming Black Friday-like traffic growth
- Agreed to run a 2-hour performance benchmark with Peregrine traffic profile and to share tuned batching/quantization recommendations
- Action items: Redwood to send 30-day pilot runbook and benchmark plan; Peregrine to provide request distribution and prompt set

Topics:
- Usage & cost trends
- Reliability incidents and mitigations
- Forecast for Q4 traffic growth and risk scenarios
- Roadmap alignment for Dedicated pilot and observability retention

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. Quick roll call — we've got Marco and Priya from Redwood, and from Peregrine Jonah, Asha, Ben and Sara, cool?
[00:06] Jonah: Yep, hi all. Sorry about the slight echo earlier, working from the office today.
[00:12] Lina: No worries. Goal for today is quick retrospective on the health metrics, then walk through the growth forecast you sent last week and align on pilot steps, timing and any procurement blockers.
[00:22] Asha: Sounds good. We also want to make sure the reliability concerns from July are fully addressed before we ramp.
[00:28] Marco: Absolutely — I'll dig into the July incident timeline briefly then we'll move into mitigations.
[00:34] 
[02:05] Marco: So July — summary: we saw a KV cache invalidation cascade after a spiky prefix pattern. In our logs the tail latency jumped, and couple of pods hit OOM on the GPU host when the sequence length spiked unexpectedly. There's a few callouts: one, prefix caching was disabled for a subset of routes; two, batching windows were tuned too aggressively for that workload and so requests batched for longer than the intended 50ms SLO.
[02:25] Ben: And that produced a 2.3x bill spike that month — our finance team flagged it.
[02:30] Marco: Right, the 2.3x is mostly tokens generated during backfill replays plus the longer average sequence length. Also a handful of fallbacks to a larger model variant because routing policy favored latency over cost in some policy rules.
[02:45] Jonah: Clarify for me — the fallback thing, that's where requests route to a 13B model instead of a smaller 7B during saturation?
[02:50] Marco: Exactly, we had a region fallback to the 13B to preserve latency which baked in higher per-token cost. We can change the policy to prefer cost during non-critical windows.
[03:01] Asha: Is that a config change? How intrusive is it to switch fallback policies?
[03:05] Priya: It's a config change in the console — low risk. We can template two policies: high-quality/low-latency and cost-preserve. We often flip between them during campaigns.
[03:18] 
[04:10] Sara: On the topic of observability, our team noticed the traces in the console didn't line up with our internal APM timestamps about 12% of the time — wondering if there's some ingestion delay?
[04:18] Marco: There can be small ingestion latencies when metrics are batched for cost efficiency. We send high-frequency traces at 1s granularity for the sampling set; everything else is approximate. I can escalate to instrumentation to tighten the sampling for your account.
[04:30] Jonah: We'd like to see token-level cost attribution mapped to routes and users — that was helpful in the pilot. Can Redwood export that as a CSV?
[04:36] Lina: Yes, we can. We'll include a sample billing breakdown in the runbook.
[04:44] 
[06:05] Marco: For mitigations: 1) re-enable prefix/KV caching for those routes, 2) reduce batching window for the sensitive routes to 30ms during business hours and increase to 150ms off-peak, 3) change fallback policy to prefer smaller model variants for non-critical traffic, 4) optionally run quantized model variant for some workloads to reduce cost ~30%.
[06:22] Ben: That quantization number — is that across-the-board or only for the generator models?
[06:27] Marco: Mostly for the generator routes; embeddings and rerankers see smaller gains. Also depends on the model family and toolkit — we have verified Q4 quant profiles for the family you run. Might be some slight quality delta — we instrument with AB tests.
[06:40] 
[08:00] Jonah: Okay, forward looking — Q4 traffic forecast shows ~4.5x spike expected during our promotional window. We're worried about both uplink latency and cost. The ask is: what's the minimum Dedicated capacity you'd recommend for a safe rollout?
[08:14] Marco: Minimal safe footprint depends on concurrency and per-request tokens. Based on the distribution you sent last week, a 4-GPU Dedicated pool (A100-class) with autoscale headroom should handle the peak with reserved throughput, plus a small hosted overflow for burst.
[08:30] Asha: How quickly can we provision a Dedicated testbed? Procurement-wise we might need to sign a short commitment.
[08:36] Lina: Typically we can provision a short-term Dedicated sandbox in 2-3 weeks once procurement approves the agreement; for production we look at 4-6 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS setup.
[08:48] Ben: Procurement will want a clear cost comparison: Hosted overflow vs Dedicated commit for the month. Can you provide that?
[08:54] Lina: Yes — that's one of the items in the runbook we'll send. We'll give modeled scenarios: baseline, 2x peak, 4.5x promo spike with both hosted and dedicated cost curves.
[09:05] 
[10:20] Sara: We also need retention and audit log detail for SOC2. What's the retention for request logs and are they exportable to our SIEM?
[10:28] Priya: Audit logs are retained per plan; by default we keep 30 days for standard plans, and we have enterprise retention add-ons to push to your S3 or GCS with 1-year or 7-year retention. Exports to SIEM are supported — we can wire a connector.
[10:40] Jonah: SSO and RBAC — we will need granular roles for model deployment and billing access.
[10:46] Marco: We support SAML/SSO, fine-grained RBAC and token scoping. We'll share a sample IAM role map for you.
[10:53] 
[12:02] Ben: On cost control — curious if Redwood supports budget alerts by route and token-type? For example, cap inference spend for the promo route to X dollars/day and auto-fallback to smaller model when threshold hits.
[12:12] Lina: Yes, route-level budgets and automatic fallback policies are available. We can wire an automated guardrail to switch routing or reject non-critical traffic when a budget threshold is met.
[12:24] Ben: Good — procurement will like that.
[12:28] 
[14:00] Marco: Quick note on the performance benchmarks: we propose a 2-hour run with your real traffic replay. We'll test three configs: hosted burst, dedicated 4-GPU baseline, and dedicated with quantized models. Metrics: p50/p95 latency, total tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M tokens. We'll need your request distribution CSV and top 100 prompt set to make the replay realistic.
[14:22] Jonah: We'll pull that together. Any specific format?
[14:25] Marco: CSV with timestamp, route, prompt_len, expected_response_len. We'll send a template.
[14:30] 
[16:10] Asha: A quick question about private deployments — if we went VPC/private, do we still get the same console features and cost analytics?
[16:18] Priya: Yes, parity feature set. There are some additional network and KMS configs but telemetry and console is same experience. Logging export might have slightly different latency due to network egress.
[16:30] Jonah: Are there any limitations on autoscaling when on-prem or in VPC?
[16:35] Marco: For on-prem we can't do the same AWS-style node autoscaling; we'd rely on your infra autoscaler, but our runtime supports elastic attach/detach and we provide guidance for headroom. For VPC-private dedicated in our cloud regions autoscale works normally.
[16:49] 
[18:00] Sara: For the AB tests on quantization, how do you measure quality regressions? We care about semantic drift, not just token overlap.
[18:08] Marco: Good point. We run prompt-level evals with your golden-set prompts and a composite quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE is not perfect) plus model-similarity and human spot checks for n samples. We feed that into our quality monitor and set regression alerts.
[18:23] Jonah: How many samples do you need for a reliable signal?
[18:26] Marco: For a baseline, 500 prompts with human review of ~50 flagged regressions gives good confidence. We'll work with your product team on the set.
[18:36] 
[20:05] Priya: Quick alignment — we've proposed two weeks of pilot (30-day cost readout) where we run a subset of traffic through Redwood Dedicated with observability turned up. That should give you a cost/latency readout and a migration playbook.
[20:20] Ben: Two weeks feels a bit short — procurement may want a month to see month-over-month variance.
[20:26] Lina: We can do 30-day pilot. The initial sandbox will be two weeks of intensified telemetry but commit to a 30-day billing window to show trends.
[20:36] Ben: Okay, makes sense.
[20:40] 
[22:10] Jonah: Any gotchas we should prepare for on network egress or encryption when setting up the dedicated pool?
[22:16] Marco: Two principal items: KMS/HSM key onboarding can take time if you're using an internal HSM provider; second, VPC peering and firewall rules for telemetry ingestion and model artifacts need whitelisting. We'll provide a checklist.
[22:30] 
[24:00] Asha: Onboarding: who will be our technical point of contact for the benchmark and pilot?
[24:05] Lina: Marco will lead the benchmark, Priya will lead operational onboarding, and I'll coordinate procurement and contract touchpoints.
[24:12] Asha: Great.
[24:20] 
[26:30] Sara: One more item — we'd like token-level cost allocated to product teams and exported daily. Any limits on partitions?
[26:38] Priya: No, we can carve cost across any number of tags or routes; we usually recommend keeping it to team, product, and environment to keep data usable. Exports can be scheduled to your S3 bucket.
[26:48] Ben: Is there sample schema for that export?
[26:51] Lina: Yes, included in the runbook.
[26:56] 
[29:05] Marco: Turning to risk scenarios for Q4: baseline +2x, +4.5x promo and a worst-case where a third-party CDN outage causes replayed traffic. In risk we recommend a hybrid approach: a reserved Dedicated pool sized for 2x baseline plus hosted overflow, and a pre-approved burst plan for the promo window. That keeps cost predictable and avoids massive fallbacks.
[29:28] Jonah: If we pre-approve burst, do you have a circuit breaker to prevent runaway spend?
[29:33] Lina: Yes, that's the budget guardrails we discussed. We can set hard caps that will automatically throttle or switch traffic to cached responses.
[29:42] 
[31:10] Asha: For the dedicated sizing you recommended, do you have a modeled cost delta vs hosted for the promo window?
[31:17] Marco: We'll show two scenarios in the runbook. As a rough ballpark, dedicated commit for heavy sustained throughput often reduces per-token cost by 35-50% versus pure hosted bursts at that scale. But there's also the fixed commit to consider.
[31:30] Ben: That 35-50% is big — good to see numbers.
[31:33] 
[33:00] Lina: Let's recap next steps so everyone's aligned. Marco will prep the benchmark plan and the replay template; Lina will send the cost runbook and sample billing breakdown; Peregrine to provide traffic CSV and prompt set; we'll tentatively schedule the benchmark the week of 2026-09-20.
[33:18] Jonah: Confirming Peregrine will share CSV by Monday the 13th.
[33:23] Ben: Procurement will try to get a decision on the short-term sandbox by the 22nd.
[33:29] Priya: We'll also draft an onboarding checklist with KMS and VPC steps and send to Asha.
[33:36] 
[35:00] Sara: One small note, earlier this week one of our microservices caused an unexpected spike when a retry loop ran — we plan to mitigate that from our side but wanted to flag that the traffic distribution may change a bit during test replay.
[35:10] Marco: Noted — for the replay we can optionally add jitter/retry artefacts to emulate that behaviour.
[35:20] Jonah: Thank you.
[35:25] 
[37:00] Lina: Any other questions or concerns?
[37:03] Asha: Nothing else from engineering.
[37:06] Ben: All good from finance for now.
[37:09] Jonah: We're good.
[37:12] Lina: Great—thanks everyone. We'll send the runbook and benchmark template today. Expect a follow-up email with dates.
[37:20] 
[41:50] End of recording.
